note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid.” The answer is no: God has not cast away the 12 tribes of Israel. “For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.” Read that first verse on the street and it tells you what the subject is about.

Paul speaks of “a remnant according to the election of grace.” Who is the elect? Isaiah says: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me.” We are the elect. Israel is the elect, not all nations. This is where Paul is getting that from.

Paul even says “God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew”: there is that word again, the same as Romans 8:29, so we did not even have to go to Amos 3; Paul deals with it here. Elijah thought he was by himself, but God answered, “I have reserved to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal.” The elect remnant is Israel.

“And so all Israel shall be saved”. And so, meaning as a result of all that has been said: all 12 tribes shall be saved. “For this is my covenant unto them”: unto the 12 tribes of Israel, the elect of Isaiah 45.

precepts.text: The continual meat offering, the continual burnt offering of the Sabbaths, of the new moons, the set feasts, the sin offerings to make an atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God. The reader must stress that: all the work of the house of our God. That's the works it's talking about. The works of the temple, the works of animal sacrifice, the offerings, and things of that nature.

Because Christians assume when Paul used the word works, Paul is talking about thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not commit adultery. No, that's not what Paul's talking about at all.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“And if by grace, then is it no more of works”. A Christian will try to hem you up with that: see, my brother, it's not about works. Christians assume that when Paul used the word works he meant thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not commit adultery. That is not what Paul is talking about at all.

Nehemiah shows what the works are: “For the shewbread, and for the continual meat offering, and for the continual burnt offering, of the sabbaths, of the new moons, for the set feasts, and for the holy things, and for the sin offerings to make an atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.”

Stress that last part: “all the work of the house of our God.” Those are the works Paul is speaking of: the works of the temple, the works of animal sacrifice, the offerings and things of that nature.

So the remnant chosen by grace is not chosen by the temple works of sacrifice and offering; it does not throw away the commandments. The elect of Israel are kept by grace, and all Israel shall be saved.

precepts.text: The Lord called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit: with the noise of a great tumult he hath kindled fire upon it, and the branches of it are broken.
precepts.point: Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be graffed in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off: Judah's unbelief caused them to be broken off. And thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear. Where did we read that? Zechariah 12:7: that they do not magnify themselves against Judah. That magnify is telling you: don't be highminded. Don't boast.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“And if some of the branches be broken off”. The branches broken off are Judah. Jeremiah shows the olive tree and its breaking: “The Lord called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit: with the noise of a great tumult he hath kindled fire upon it, and the branches of it are broken.”

God himself named his people a green olive tree, fair and of goodly fruit. That is the tree Paul speaks of. And the fire kindled on it with a great tumult is how the branches came to be broken.

Why were they broken? Paul answers: “because of unbelief they were broken off”. Judah's unbelief caused them to be broken off.

So when the wild olive tree, the northern kingdom, is graffed in among them, it is graffed into God's own green olive tree. “Boast not against the branches”: do not boast against Judah. “thou bearest not the root, but the root thee”. The root is Christ, and Christ is the one that keeps the northern kingdom graffed in with Judah. “Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.”

precepts.text: Take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah; then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim; and join them one to another into one stick. That's the grafting: and they shall become one in thine hand.
precepts.point: Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be graffed in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off: Judah's unbelief caused them to be broken off. And thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear. Where did we read that? Zechariah 12:7: that they do not magnify themselves against Judah. That magnify is telling you: don't be highminded. Don't boast.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them”. That is what Ezekiel 37 shows: “Moreover, thou son of man, take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions”.

“And join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand.” That is the grafting: the stick of Joseph, Ephraim and the house of Israel, joined to the stick of Judah, and the two become one in God's hand.

So the wild olive tree is not the nations; it is the northern kingdom being joined back with Judah. That is why Paul warns, “Boast not against the branches.” Zechariah 12:7 says the same: that they do not magnify themselves against Judah. That magnify is telling you: do not be highminded, do not boast.

“Be not highminded, but fear”. The root that bears the graffed-in branch is Christ, and he is the one that holds the two sticks together as one.

precepts.text: Why did Paul open with, Hath God cast away his people? Because of the northern and southern kingdom conflict: the Jews thought God was not dealing with the northern kingdom. I would not that ye should be ignorant of this mystery: blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in; God blinded a portion so the gospel could be preached to the northern kingdom living as Gentiles. And so all Israel shall be saved means both kingdoms, all twelve tribes, can be saved. It is not a license saying the wicked escape hell; that is not what Paul was talking about.
precepts.point: But thou art cast out of thy grave like an abominable branch: this is the future of the pride of America.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

precepts.why:
Some Israelite camps use “all Israel shall be saved” to argue that even the wicked will escape hell. To see what Paul meant, start from the beginning of the chapter: “I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.”

Why did Paul open that way? Because of the conflict between the northern and southern kingdoms. The Jews thought God was not dealing with the northern kingdom anymore, since God had told them, you are not my people, and Hosea said that where it was said unto them, you are not my people, there they would be called the children of the living God. Paul, of Benjamin, was of the southern kingdom, and he answers, “God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.”

“For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.” The mystery is that God is dealing with both the northern and southern kingdoms, which is why the chapter talks about them being grafted back in. God blinded a portion, the Jews, to salvation in Jesus Christ so that the gospel could be preached to the northern kingdom living as Gentiles, so they could come in. If you say you're an Israelite and you still don't understand this chapter after all these years, you're an idiot, and God is not dealing with you.

“And so all Israel shall be saved”. That means both kingdoms, all twelve tribes, can be saved. It is not a license saying a murderer, an adulterer or a thief will be saved at the end no matter what. You see how stupid they are? Leaders who use this verse to say you are not going to hell are wise in their own conceits. There is a hell, and if you go against God you are going into it, Israelite or not.

precepts.text: Hath God cast away his people? God forbid; for I also am an Israelite, of the tribe of Benjamin. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew: Amos 3 and Romans 8 again.
precepts.point: Moreover the law entered, that the offence might abound: the law was introduced so sin could be understood and exposed, thou shalt not covet, thou shalt not commit adultery, to guide a naturally sinful people. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound: keeping the commandments we realize how much we rise, fall, and stumble and how much more grace we need than under Moses, where animals could not atone for everything. That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
If sin reigned unto death over the chosen line, has God given up on them? Paul answers: “I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.”

“God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.” Which he foreknew: that is Amos 3 and Romans 8 again. “You only have I known of all the families of the earth”, and “whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate”.

The cycle Ezra described, the righteous line receiving the law, going off, being destroyed and repenting, never ended with God throwing his people away. Every time, out of that line the righteous rose up again.

So where sin abounded, grace did much more abound, and it abounded upon the same people God foreknew. Paul, an Israelite of Benjamin, is himself the proof that God has not cast away his people.

precepts.text: For the shewbread, the continual meat offering, the burnt offering, the sabbaths, new moons and set feasts, the sin offerings to make an atonement for Israel, and all the work of the house of our God. These are the works of Romans 11:6.
precepts.point: If the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world: reconcile means bringing back together what was together before, and the nations were never together with us. Isaiah 45:17 calls Israel the world without end, and Mark 10:30 speaks of the world to come. The receiving of them will be life from the dead, as Ephesians 2:1 says of those dead in trespasses and sins.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Romans 11:5 speaks of “a remnant according to the election of grace”, and verse 6 goes on: “And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace.” If by grace, meaning Christ's death, his mercy: Christ's death granted us grace, his sacrifice granted us grace. So what are the works? Nehemiah shows them.

“For the shewbread, and for the continual meat offering, and for the continual burnt offering, of the sabbaths, of the new moons, for the set feasts, and for the holy things, and for the sin offerings to make an atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.” The works are the sacrifices and temple ordinances, which were still around when Paul wrote the letter, because the temple had not yet been destroyed. Israel was still doing them.

So “no more of works” means no more sacrifice. We are not being called based upon animals we sacrifice; we are being called based upon our acceptance of Christ's death on the cross and of him being the Messiah. It is no more of works once Christ died.

“otherwise grace is no more grace”: if we are still regarding and accepting the sacrificing of animals, then Christ's death is void. Then we put Christ to the back and just keep sacrificing animals. “But if it be of works, then is it no more grace”: then you put Christ out of the way, no more Messiah. “otherwise work is no more work”: the sacrifice is done away with, because Christ died on the cross.

precepts.text: Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation, world without end. Israel is the world.
precepts.point: If the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world: reconcile means bringing back together what was together before, and the nations were never together with us. Isaiah 45:17 calls Israel the world without end, and Mark 10:30 speaks of the world to come. The receiving of them will be life from the dead, as Ephesians 2:1 says of those dead in trespasses and sins.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Romans 11:12 says “Now if the fall of them be the riches of the world, and the diminishing of them the riches of the Gentiles”. The fall of them is the builders, the leaders of the southern kingdom, rejecting Christ, and the diminishing is the same thing in different wording: something that decays, drops lower, falls. What are the riches of the world? Is it talking about money? No: the kingdom. The Pharisees had to reject Christ because it was their lot; Christ had to be killed, and once he died on that cross he granted us access to the kingdom. That is the riches of the world.

And who is the world? Some say, world is Israel, where did you get that from? World is world. No, it's not. The world is us: “But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.” Israel is the world without end.

Christ says the same in Mark 10:30: “in the world to come eternal life.” The world to come is our kingdom, eternal life. That is the riches of the world.

So when Romans 11:15 says “if the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world”, it is speaking of Israel. To reconcile is to bring back together what was together before, and the nations were never together with us.

precepts.text: The Lord shall save the tents of Judah first. Romans 1:16 and 2:9 say the same: to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
precepts.point: If the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world: reconcile means bringing back together what was together before, and the nations were never together with us. Isaiah 45:17 calls Israel the world without end, and Mark 10:30 speaks of the world to come. The receiving of them will be life from the dead, as Ephesians 2:1 says of those dead in trespasses and sins.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Romans 11:11 says the leaders' fall brought salvation to the Gentiles “for to provoke them to jealousy”, as Moses said: “I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people”. The ones provoked are the southern kingdom, and the ones who are no people are the northern kingdom, who received Christ. But the southern kingdom still comes first.

“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” He will raise the tents of Judah first.

Paul says it too: the gospel of Christ “is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.” The Jew is Judah, first; the Greek is the northern kingdom. And judgment runs in the same order: “Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile”.

That is why Romans 11 says God has not cast away his people. Judah stumbled, but Judah is saved first, and the northern kingdom that received Christ provokes them to jealousy until they come in.

precepts.text: When the Jews saw the multitudes they were filled with envy. Paul said it was necessary the word should first be spoken to you, but seeing ye put it from you, lo, we turn to the Gentiles. Paul went to the northern kingdom, not the Arabs or the Chinese.
precepts.point: If the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world: reconcile means bringing back together what was together before, and the nations were never together with us. Isaiah 45:17 calls Israel the world without end, and Mark 10:30 speaks of the world to come. The receiving of them will be life from the dead, as Ephesians 2:1 says of those dead in trespasses and sins.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Here is Romans 11:11 happening in history. “But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with envy”: that is Judah, filled with jealousy. They “spake against those things which were spoken by Paul, contradicting and blaspheming.”

“Then Paul and Barnabas waxed bold, and said, It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you”: to the southern kingdom, first. “but seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles.” They rejected it, so Paul turned to the Gentiles, who are not a people: the northern kingdom.

You won't find it in the Bible that Israel rejected the prophets and the prophets went to the Arabs. Isaiah never said, they reject me, I'm going to go talk to the Philistines. Lo, we turn to the East Indians, lo, we turn to the Chinese? Christ is black and you're not, there are twelve gates and your name's not on them, but serve him anyway? That makes no sense. Whether you are a black Hebrew Israelite or a Christian, if you teach that, you hate your people. He showeth his word unto Jacob and has not dealt so with any other nation, and still you look for some way to save the people who destroyed, raped, robbed and murdered your people, and don't want judgment to come to them.

So the Gentiles Paul turned to were his own flesh, the northern kingdom, “for to provoke them to jealousy”, that he might “provoke to emulation them which are my flesh, and might save some of them.”

precepts.text: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ's at his coming.
precepts.point: As concerning the gospel they are enemies for your sakes, but as touching the election they are beloved for the fathers' sakes. As ye in times past had not believed God but now have obtained mercy through their unbelief, so they through your mercy may obtain mercy. God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all: all Israel.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
“For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy”. Who is the firstfruit? Paul answers it in Corinthians: “But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming.”

Christ is the firstfruits. It starts with Christ, because he is our creator, the rock that begat us, and then it goes to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob as well. “Afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming” means the elect.

And the lump is Israel. If the firstfruit is holy, the lump is also holy: because Christ is holy, the people that come after him in his order are holy too.

So Romans 11 opens by tying Israel to Christ. The same holy firstfruit stands at the head of the whole lump, and that is why God has not cast away his people. Both kingdoms, the branches that fell and the branches grafted back in, belong to that holy lump that follows Christ.

precepts.text: I am the root and the offspring of David.
precepts.point: As concerning the gospel they are enemies for your sakes, but as touching the election they are beloved for the fathers' sakes. As ye in times past had not believed God but now have obtained mercy through their unbelief, so they through your mercy may obtain mercy. God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all: all Israel.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
“And if the root be holy, so are the branches.” Who is the root? Christ says it himself: “I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David”.

And who are the branches? Christ said in John 15, “I am the vine, ye are the branches.” The branches go into the offspring, the children: us. If the root is holy, so are the branches that grow out of him.

That is what “the root and fatness of the olive tree” is in verse 17. Both kingdoms partake of Christ; he rules over them both. And it is why Paul warns, “Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee.” If you boast against your brothers, you are not following Christ; it is Christ, the root, that bears you.

So the root being holy is the reason the natural branches can be grafted in again and the wild branches can be grafted in at all. Everything grows out of Christ, the root and offspring of David.

precepts.text: They are gone up to Assyria, a wild ass alone by himself.
precepts.point: As concerning the gospel they are enemies for your sakes, but as touching the election they are beloved for the fathers' sakes. As ye in times past had not believed God but now have obtained mercy through their unbelief, so they through your mercy may obtain mercy. God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all: all Israel.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
“And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them”. The branches broken off are the southern kingdom, because they stumbled and fell. Who is the “thou”, the wild olive tree? The northern kingdom.

Hosea shows why Ephraim is called wild: “For they are gone up to Assyria, a wild ass alone by himself: Ephraim hath hired lovers.” Ephraim is a wild ass alone by himself; a wild ass or a wild olive tree, it is the northern kingdom gone off into idolatry.

That is why Paul, speaking as the apostle of the Gentiles, writes to the southern kingdom while also addressing the northern kingdom: you that I am writing to were also a wild olive tree. And that is why the grafting is “contrary to nature”: the northern kingdom was uncircumcised, in uncleanness, scattered abroad afar off, not a people, and hated by the southern kingdom.

Grafting in goes into reconciling: bringing the two back together again. You can only graft an olive tree into an olive tree; you cannot graft a mango tree into an olive tree. The wild branches are the same kind as the natural ones: Israel.

precepts.text: The Lord called thy name a green olive tree; he hath kindled fire upon it and the branches of it are broken, for the evil of the house of Israel and of the house of Judah.
precepts.point: As concerning the gospel they are enemies for your sakes, but as touching the election they are beloved for the fathers' sakes. As ye in times past had not believed God but now have obtained mercy through their unbelief, so they through your mercy may obtain mercy. God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all: all Israel.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Who is the olive tree? Jeremiah shows it: “The Lord called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit: with the noise of a great tumult he hath kindled fire upon it, and the branches of it are broken.” The branches of it are broken, just as Paul referenced.

Then watch who that olive tree is: “For the Lord of hosts, that planted thee, hath pronounced evil against thee, for the evil of the house of Israel and of the house of Judah, which they have done against themselves to provoke me to anger in offering incense unto Baal.” The house of Israel first, the house of Judah second: both houses.

So the olive tree refers to both the house of Israel and the house of Judah. The wild olive tree is not the other nations; the nations are never called olive trees.

That is how Romans 11 ends: “God is able to graff them in again.” Again, because they were always there. “And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.” Their sins, Jacob’s sins, all twelve tribes. The white man did many sins on this earth, and the Lord is not taking his sins away; he is going to pay for them. “God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all”: all Israel.

precepts.text: And so all Israel shall be saved: there shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob.
precepts.point: Respect unto His chosen is not respect of persons. Within Israel there is no respect of persons: the Most High renders to every man according to his deeds, tribulation and anguish upon every soul that doeth evil, of the Jew first and also of the Gentile, the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom that was Hellenized; but glory, honour, and peace to every man that worketh good. The nation is chosen above the nations, and all Israel shall be saved through the Deliverer out of Sion.

note.label: Exodus 2: The Birth of Moses

precepts.why:
God heard their groaning, remembered his covenant, and had respect unto them, and the end of that respect is written: “And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob”.

The nation is chosen above the nations, and all Israel shall be saved through the Deliverer out of Sion, who turns away ungodliness from Jacob. The cry that came up unto God by reason of the bondage is answered in him.

precepts.text: Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
precepts.point: Test that against the doctrine that says the Most High cast off Israel after Christ. Paul, whose writings that doctrine misinterprets, said the same thing Samuel said.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
“For the Lord will not forsake his people for his great name’s sake: because it hath pleased the Lord to make you his people.” That is part of the comfort of the scriptures: he may purge his people, but he will never exterminate the Israelites, for his name’s sake.

Test that against the doctrine that says the Most High cast off Israel after Christ. Paul, whose writings that doctrine misinterprets, asks the question himself: “Hath God cast away his people? God forbid.” And he gives himself as the proof: “For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.” Paul said the same thing Samuel said.

precepts.text: God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew; the Lord has not cast off Israel.
precepts.point: Test that against the doctrine that says the Most High cast off Israel after Christ. Paul, whose writings that doctrine misinterprets, said the same thing Samuel said.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
Paul goes on: “God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.” The Lord has not cast off Israel.

It pleased the Lord to make Israel his people in Samuel’s day, and after Christ they are still the people which he foreknew. He will not forsake them, for his great name’s sake.

precepts.text: Paul says God hath not cast away His people whom He foreknew, for Paul himself is an Israelite of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
precepts.point: The Most High will not cast off His people nor forsake His inheritance. People say black people are gentiles and nationality is not important, but this tells you nationality is extremely important; you must know who you are.

note.label: Psalm 94: The God of Vengeance and Defense of His People

precepts.why:
“For the Lord will not cast off his people, neither will he forsake his inheritance.” Paul asks the question straight: “I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.”

Paul says God has not cast away his people whom he foreknew, and his proof is himself: an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. He knew his nationality and his tribe. He goes on to Elias, who “maketh intercession to God against Israel, saying, Lord, they have killed thy prophets, and digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life”, and still God had not cast them off.

People say black people are gentiles and nationality is not important, but this tells you nationality is extremely important; you must know who you are. Blessed is the man whom the Most High chastens and teaches out of his law; that is why in Revelation the books are opened and the book of your life is measured against the laws. He chastens his people, but he does not cast them off.

precepts.text: Israel will never be cast off; the Most High has not cast away His people whom He foreknew.
precepts.point: They that trust in the Most High shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed but abideth forever. As the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so the Most High is round about His people from henceforth even forever, which goes and shows that Israel will never be cast off.

note.label: Psalm 125: They That Trust Shall Be As Mount Zion

precepts.why:
“I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.” Israel will never be cast off; the Most High has not cast away his people whom he foreknew.

That is what “As the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so the Lord is round about his people from henceforth even for ever” goes and shows. They that trust in the Most High are as mount Zion, which cannot be removed but abideth for ever. And however he leads forth those who turn aside to their crooked ways with the workers of iniquity, always remember: “peace shall be upon Israel.”

precepts.text: When Christ came teaching, the word was a snare and a trap to the leadership of the southern kingdom.
precepts.point: The word became a snare upon the leadership because the understanding is given precept upon precept, in another tongue, so that those without it stumble and fall.

note.label: Isaiah 8: Maher-shalal-hash-baz, the Snare, and the Law and the Testimony

precepts.why:
The rock of offence and the snare came upon the leadership when Christ came teaching. Paul brings David: “And David saith, Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumblingblock, and a recompence unto them”.

When Christ came teaching, the word was a snare and a trap to the leadership of the southern kingdom, the inhabitants of Jerusalem. Their table, the word given precept upon precept, became a stumblingblock and a recompence unto them, the very gin and snare Isaiah spoke of.

precepts.text: The precept that God has not cast away his people whom he foreknew, the seed of Abraham.
precepts.point: Fear thou not, for I am with thee; I will strengthen thee and uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness. All that were incensed against Israel shall be ashamed and confounded, be as nothing, and perish; those that war against Israel shall be as a thing of naught.

note.label: Isaiah 41: Israel My Servant, the Chosen Seed

precepts.why:
“But thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend”, and “I have chosen thee, and not cast thee away.” Paul asks and answers the same thing: “I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.”

God has not cast away his people, the seed of Abraham, and Paul proves it by himself: an Israelite, of the tribe of Benjamin. When the New Testament speaks of the chosen and the servants, it is talking about Israel; the servants of God are Israelites and the chosen of God are Israelites, all twelve tribes, not everybody. The Most High took Israel from the ends of the earth and said, “Thou art my servant”, and he holds Israel’s right hand, saying, “Fear not; I will help thee.”

precepts.text: God has not cast away His people whom He foreknew, and we are the living proof, our hearts turned back to keeping the commandments and the faith of Christ without bodily eyes having seen Him.
precepts.point: He tells Jeremiah not to regard the people who say the two families the Most High chose He has now cast off and despised so they should be no more a nation; if His covenant with day and night stands, He will not cast away the seed of Jacob and David.

note.label: Jeremiah 33: The Branch of Righteousness and the Covenant of Day and Night

precepts.why:
The people said the two families the Lord had chosen “he hath even cast them off”, that they should be no more a nation. The Lord answers that as surely as his covenant with day and night stands, he will not cast away the seed of Jacob and David. Paul asks the same question and gives the same answer: “I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.”

God has not cast away his people whom he foreknew, and we are the living proof. Our hearts are turned back to keeping the commandments and the faith of Christ without our bodily eyes ever having seen him. The covenant with David that he should not want a son to reign upon his throne, and the seed of David and the Levites multiplied like the host of heaven and the sand of the sea, stand as sure as day and night in their season, for he will cause our captivity to return and have mercy on us.

precepts.text: Israel obtained not that which he seeketh for, and the rest were blinded, and their table was made a snare and a trap unto them.
precepts.point: The same men who could quote where he would be born were blinded when he walked among them. Knowing the book is not the same as seeing the one the book speaks of.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

precepts.why:
The same men who could quote where he would be born were blinded when he walked among them. Paul explains it: “Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for; but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded (According as it is written, God hath given them the spirit of slumber, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear;) unto this day.”

Israel sought the messiah and did not obtain him; the election obtained it, and the rest were blinded, given the spirit of slumber and eyes that should not see. Then Paul brings David: “Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumblingblock, and a recompence unto them: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back alway.” Their table was made a snare and a trap unto them. The chief priests and scribes had the table set before them and it snared them: knowing the book is not the same as seeing the one the book speaks of.

precepts.text: The Most High gave the rest the spirit of slumber and let their table be a snare; not everyone reads and understands the same, because it is spiritual.
precepts.point: David himself did not ascend, but said the Most High told his Lord to sit at his right hand until his foes are made his footstool, another prophecy pointing to Christ.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
The rest were blinded: “God hath given them the spirit of slumber, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear;) unto this day.” And David said, “Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumblingblock, and a recompence unto them”.

Not everyone reads and understands the same, because it is spiritual. The apostles were witnesses whose understanding was opened, while the rest had the spirit of slumber. That is why some heard Peter prove Christ from David and saw it, and others did not.

precepts.text: As concerning the gospel they are enemies for your sakes, but as touching the election they are beloved for the fathers' sakes, because they can still repent.
precepts.point: This is the true meaning of loving your enemies. Christianity twists it to mean love the ones who enslaved, raped, and colonized your ancestors, stole your nationality, land, and heritage, miseducated you, gave you a false image of God, and today shut down anyone who says Israel is the true children of God. That is not the enemy the scripture means. The Bible means love the enemies within your own nation, because Paul, who persecuted and killed the disciples, was one of those enemies who could still repent.

note.label: Acts 9: A Chosen Vessel

precepts.why:
“As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the fathers’ sakes.” Enemies as concerning the gospel, yet beloved as touching the election, because they can still repent. That is the enemy Christ meant when he said love your enemies: the enemy within your own nation.

Saul was exactly that. He held authority from the chief priests to bind all that called on the name, an enemy of the gospel, and yet beloved for the fathers' sakes, and he repented. Not the ones who enslaved and colonized your ancestors, but your own people who fight the truth, may still come to it.

precepts.text: Paul answers plainly, "I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin," so his Roman citizenship never made him a Roman by nation.
precepts.point: Because the Israelites were scattered through every province and took the names of their captivities, scholars cannot tell a Roman Jewish soldier from a Roman by his name alone, and the New Testament was written in Greek because Israel spoke Greek under the Greeks. Correcting a misheard reference to Luke 3, the centurions of scripture were often Israelite servants in the army.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
The same Paul who told the chief captain he was a Roman answers plainly: “I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.”

His Roman citizenship never made him a Roman by nation. That is how to read Cornelius: a Roman officer by his post and his name, and an Israelite by his seed.

precepts.text: The wild olive tree is grafted in among the branches and partakes of the root, but is warned not to boast, for the branches were broken off through unbelief.
precepts.point: Ephraim is the wild olive tree grafted back in among the tribes, partaking of the root and fatness, and Paul warns them not to boast against the branches. The north believed on Christ while much of the south, the Pharisees, stumbled at him, but that is no ground to boast.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Ephraim is the wild olive tree grafted back in among the tribes: “thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches.”

The north believed on Christ while much of the south, the Pharisees, stumbled at him. “Because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith.” But that is no ground to boast: “Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.”

That is what the circumcision saw in Cornelius' house: the wild olive grafted back in, receiving the same Holy Ghost, speaking with tongues, which were known languages, not unknown, as in Acts 2. So Peter asked, “Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we?” and commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.why: They're enemies of the gospel. They can repent, though, because they are beloved. But if they don't repent: “But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul: all they that hate me love death.” So Christ said, if you hate me, you love death. That's a cold deal right there.

moments.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers
The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

points: I say then, hath God cast away his people? God forbid. The answer is no. God has not cast away the 12 tribes of Israel. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. Once you read that on the street, that first verse tells you what the subject is about.
And so all Israel shall be saved: and so, meaning as a result of all that I said. All 12 tribes shall be saved. For this is my covenant unto them: unto them who? The 12 tribes of Israel.
God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew: there's that word again. So we didn't even have to go to Amos 3; Paul deals with it here in Romans 11:2.

Elijah thought he was by himself. But what saith the answer of God unto him? I have reserved to myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal. Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.

And if by grace, then is it no more of works: now a Christian will try to hem you up with that. See, it's not about works, my brother. Because Christians assume when Paul used the word works, Paul is talking about thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not commit adultery. No, that's not what Paul's talking about at all.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: And if some of the branches be broken off: that's Judah broken off. And thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them: that's what we just read in Ezekiel 37.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: Boast not against the branches: don't boast against Judah. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee: the root is Christ. Christ is the one that keeps the northern kingdom graffed in with Judah.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be graffed in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off: Judah's unbelief caused them to be broken off. And thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear. Where did we read that? Zechariah 12:7: that they do not magnify themselves against Judah. That magnify is telling you: don't be highminded. Don't boast.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: With all this, they have something called Christian dispensationalism, or replacement theology: that God's people are done away with. I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. Paul was dealing with that back then. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin: Paul was proving the Israelites were not done away with.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

points: All Israel shall be saved, southern and northern kingdom. There shall come out of Zion the Deliverer, Christ, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob; this is my covenant when I take away their sins. Start at verse 26 on the street, because it explains the whole chapter.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

points: As concerning the gospel they are enemies for your sakes: the ones who made a covenant with Rome and Babylon, religious or political. But as touching the election they are beloved for the fathers' sakes, because they can still repent. The gifts and calling of God are without repentance; he died for us before we were there.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

points: Hath God cast away his people? God forbid, for I also am an Israelite of the tribe of Benjamin. He has not cast away his people which he foreknew. As in Elijah's day, when God reserved seven thousand who had not bowed to Baal, there is a remnant according to the election of grace. When the Bible and street teaching are outlawed, we will see who has not bowed.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

points: If by grace, then it is no more of works. The works are the sacrifices and temple ordinances of Nehemiah 10:33, still running when Paul wrote. Acceptance of Christ's death, not animal sacrifice, is the ground of the calling; to go back to sacrifice makes grace no more grace.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

points: Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for, but the election hath obtained it and the rest were blinded: the leaders, given a spirit of slumber, their table a snare, their eyes darkened, as David wrote.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

points: Have they stumbled that they should fall for ever? God forbid: through their fall salvation is come unto the Gentiles, the northern kingdom, to provoke them to jealousy, exactly as Moses said. Paul magnifies his office as apostle to the Gentiles to provoke to emulation them which are his flesh, the southern kingdom.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

points: If the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world: reconcile means bringing back together what was together before, and the nations were never together with us. Isaiah 45:17 calls Israel the world without end, and Mark 10:30 speaks of the world to come. The receiving of them will be life from the dead, as Ephesians 2:1 says of those dead in trespasses and sins.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

points: If the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy; if the root be holy, so are the branches. Christ is the firstfruits, the root and offspring of David, and the vine; we are the branches.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

points: Thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them. Hosea calls Ephraim a wild ass alone by himself, and Jeremiah 11:16 names both the house of Israel and the house of Judah as God's olive tree, with broken branches. The nations are never called olive trees.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

points: Boast not against the branches. Ephraim might say the branches were broken off so I could be graffed in; well, because of unbelief they were broken off and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded but fear, for if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he spare not thee.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

points: God is able to graff them in again. Again, because they were there before. If the wild branch can be graffed contrary to nature, how much more the natural branches into their own olive tree.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

points: Blindness in part is happened to Israel until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in, and so all Israel shall be saved; the Deliverer shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob, for this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins. Jacob's sins, not Esau's; the white man pays for his.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

points: As concerning the gospel they are enemies for your sakes, but as touching the election they are beloved for the fathers' sakes. As ye in times past had not believed God but now have obtained mercy through their unbelief, so they through your mercy may obtain mercy. God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all: all Israel.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

points: The gifts and calling of God are without repentance. God calls people as they are, but once they learn, they must put away adultery, fornication and lust.

note.label: America Hedgemony & Oppression

points: We get on to Christians a lot, and rightfully so, because right now, in this state of mind that they're in, they're no damn good. We're going here because Luke 19:27 says "but those mine enemies": who are the enemies of today? Here it goes. “And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer,” That's Christ. “and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.”

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

points: Here comes the point. “As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes:” Those are the unbelievers. Those that are in other religions, they are our enemies, brothers and sisters throughout our people that disbelieve. Like at the time when Paul wrote that, our enemies were the scribes, Pharisees and Sadducees.

“but as touching the election, they are beloved for the fathers’ sakes.” How are they going to be our enemies and be beloved? Because they are part of the elect, God's elected people, they are Israel, they are still our people whatever doctrine they're with; but that misses it. They're beloved because, even though they're still part of the election, they can still repent for the things that they've done. That's what you miss: they can still repent. Think about the Apostle Paul. Wasn't he an enemy to the gospel? But the Lord allowed him to repent. As wicked as our brothers and sisters are in Islam and Christianity, they are still beloved for the fathers' sakes because they can repent. They can wake up one day and say, "You know what? Them Israelites is right. I've been fighting them all this time, but they're right, and I need to shut my black lips and repent." That's the prayer.

Some of these people, and I'm not pointing fingers, some of them are lesbians. Some of them are sodomites, homosexuals. Don't follow these people. And they all love the white man. They all love Esau above you. Then the urban apologists: they are the enemies of the gospel, brothers and sisters. Look at the one on the left, the black fat man with the white man; this is their love for the white man. And they love talking about Afrocentricity; they talk about black church fathers like Tertullian. The hell with that sellout Tertullian who loved Rome, loved the white man. The white ones are just called apologists, but they call the black ones urban apologists; you know what urban is another word for. Some of these are TikTok people; that guy in the center, I don't even know his name, but I see him running his black lips a lot. The fat chick on the right has a project called Jude 3, which tries to exalt blackness, but they hate the Bible the way the Israelites teach it; they hate a black Christ: "No, we're not the twelve tribes. We're African." Where's the African in the Bible? Losers, bums. They despise when we say things like the Bible is a black man's book, the gospel is about black liberation. They cringe to hear that.
